summary:
Our project is an interactive space survival game designed to teach children how astronauts manage a lunar or Martian outpost. Players take on the role of mission commanders, making important decisions about limited resources such as oxygen, energy, food, and radiation protection. Each decision has consequences: using more power for research may reduce energy available for life support, while improving radiation shielding may consume valuable resources.

The game transforms complex space engineering challenges into an enjoyable and educational experience for children aged 7–12. By combining interactive gameplay with real NASA data, it helps players understand the challenges of living beyond Earth, develop problem-solving and critical-thinking skills, and discover the science behind space exploration. Our goal is to make learning about space more engaging while showing that every decision matters for a successful mission.

Project Details

Our project is an interactive space survival and resource management game that allows children to experience what it takes to manage a human outpost on the Moon or Mars. Players become mission commanders responsible for keeping astronauts alive by managing essential resources such as oxygen, energy, food, and radiation protection.

The game works through interactive decisions and challenges. Every choice has consequences: using more energy for scientific research may leave less power for life support, while improving radiation shielding may consume resources needed for food production. Players must think strategically, solve problems, and balance competing priorities to keep their outpost running successfully.

Benefits and Intended Impact: Our project makes complex space engineering concepts easier and more enjoyable for children aged 7–12. It encourages critical thinking, problem-solving, scientific curiosity, and an understanding of the challenges of human space exploration. We aim to inspire the next generation of scientists, engineers, and astronauts.

Tools and Technologies: The project is developed using [insert your actual programming languages, frameworks, software, and tools]. AI tools such as ChatGPT were used to assist with brainstorming, explanations, and development where applicable.

Creativity and Innovation: Instead of simply teaching facts about space, our project turns real mission challenges into an interactive learning experience. Players learn through experimentation, decision-making, and experiencing the consequences of their choices.

Design Considerations: We considered the target age group, accessibility, simple language, engaging gameplay, educational accuracy, resource limitations, and replayability. Our main goal is to combine entertainment with meaningful scientific learning and demonstrate that every decision matters when humans live beyond Earth.
